page: Amazon Web Services c8gb.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Graviton family featuring ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores. The configuration provides 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz with a 1:1 thread-to-core mapping under the Nitro hypervisor. Cache architecture consists of 64 KB L1 data cache per core, 2 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is 8.0 GB, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The instance does not include bundled local storage or hardware accelerators, relying on remote network storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the c8gb.xlarge primarily within the middle tier across standard system tests. In Geekbench testing, the instance achieved a single-core score of 1869.0 and a multi-core score of 5887.0, with consistent middle-tier scores across Clang compilation, ray tracing, and image processing. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression reached 14.4 GB/sec, placing in the top quartile of results. However, cryptographic and vector benchmarks expose architectural boundaries; PassMark encryption scores fell into the bottom decile at 754.28, reflecting missing x86 instruction extensions such as AVX-512 and AMX. LLM inference benchmarks demonstrated weak token throughput, indicating limited suitability for machine learning model serving.

Given its 1:2 memory-to-vCPU allocation and dedicated ARM physical execution cores, the c8gb.xlarge is tailored for compute-bound tasks requiring predictable execution without thread contention. It shows stable performance for in-memory caching with 9.23 million Redis SET operations per second and static web throughput of 10.11 GB/sec. The instance delivers cost-effective compute capacity for microservices, continuous integration build runners, batch data compression pipelines, and distributed web applications where local disk and heavy vectorized floating-point extensions are not prerequisites.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gb.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance based on the 64-bit ARMv9 architecture, running AWS Neoverse-V2 Graviton processors. It features 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, clocked at 2.8 GHz, supported by 8.0 GB of system memory and 36 MB of L3 cache. The instance operates on the Nitro hypervisor, incorporates 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and does not include local disk storage or GPU accelerators. In synthetic and application benchmarks, the server demonstrates solid performance in data decompression and stable throughput in web serving and Redis caching, while displaying lower comparative results in cryptographic workloads and LLM inference. With a lean 2 GB per core ratio, c8gb.xlarge provides an efficient hardware footprint for continuous integration pipelines, batch processing, static web serving, and microservices architectures requiring dedicated core execution.
